children.name: Prior Art and Clearance Searching
children.blurb: Prior art and clearance searching is the practice of finding earlier patents, publications, trademarks, and other disclosures that affect whether an invention is patentable or a mark is registrable and usable.

children.name: Trademark Filing and Specimens
children.blurb: Trademark filing and specimens covers the steps and evidence needed to register a mark with a trademark office.

children.name: Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness
children.blurb: Licensing synthetic assets and likeness covers the rights to use AI-generated or AI-modified representations of a person, including face, voice, name, image, and distinctive style.

children.name: Patent Claim Drafting
children.blurb: Patent claim drafting is the part of patent prosecution that turns a technical disclosure into the precise legal language that defines an invention.

children.name: Infringement Detection and Enforcement
children.blurb: Infringement detection and enforcement covers the work of finding unauthorized use of trademarks, copyrights, and related rights, then deciding what action to take.

sections.body: Intellectual property and trademark strategy in AI covers two connected jobs: using AI systems to search, draft, file, license and enforce rights, and sorting out who owns or can use the outputs, data and likenesses that AI systems produce. In practice, AI is doing clearance searching across patent and trademark databases, grouping similar marks, flagging confusingly similar goods and services, and drafting first-pass patent claims. It is also used to monitor marketplaces and social platforms for counterfeit listings, copycat packaging and unauthorized use of protected material. On the licensing side, teams use AI to track synthetic assets, voice clones, digital replicas and other generated content that may need permission or a contract. The work is not autonomous legal practice. It is document-heavy, pattern-heavy support that still lands on a lawyer, agent or rights holder to review.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is partly solved at the search and monitoring layer. AI can retrieve prior art, compare trademark records and surface likely infringement at a scale no manual review can match, and this site tracks 149 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how quickly disputes are reaching courts. What is not solved is the legal core: ownership of AI-assisted inventions, the scope of rights in synthetic assets, the evidentiary weight of AI-generated specimens, and the line between inspiration and infringement. Patent claim drafting tools can propose language and variations, but claim scope, enablement and written description still depend on human judgment and the specific disclosure. Trademark filing still turns on actual use, specimens and goods and services descriptions, and AI can misread those if the record is thin. Enforcement is also uneven, because detection tools produce leads and false positives, not proof. The honest limit is that AI speeds up preparation and review, but it does not decide registrability, patentability, infringement or fair use.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the life of an IP matter. Prior Art and Clearance Searching is the entry point for freedom to operate and registrability checks, where a reader goes to understand how AI searches patent, trademark and non-patent literature before a filing or launch. Trademark Filing and Specimens covers the prosecution side, including how AI helps prepare applications, classify goods and services and test whether a specimen shows use in commerce. Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness deals with contracts and permissions around generated content, digital replicas and persona rights, which is where AI output meets ownership and consent questions. Patent Claim Drafting focuses on the language of claims and the limits of automated drafting, while Infringement Detection and Enforcement covers monitoring, evidence gathering and the decision to send a notice or file suit. Read together, they show a workflow that starts with search, moves through filing and licensing, and ends in detection and enforcement, with human review at every step.
